## Highlights

- A task whose agent runs on Claude Code no longer runs out of starts while its model is at capacity. When the provider refuses a turn with HTTP 503, as a gateway does when every account behind it is at its limit, or with 529, as Anthropic does when it is overloaded, the run now waits for the model instead of failing. So does every task run of the organization started on that model meanwhile: they read **Waiting for model capacity**, take no worker, and start again in waves once the model answers. The refused run's automatic retry uses no attempt and does not count toward the task's three automatic starts an hour. Before this release, each such refusal used one of each, and once they ran out the task stayed **In progress** with no run, and dispatch did not start it again. An automation's agent step refused this way now retries a minute later instead of at once, still as one of its three retries. A 429, which is one account's rate limit, is handled as before, and so is every other status ([#5348](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5348)). See [Handle waiting and failed runs](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/projects/task-automation#handle-waiting-and-failed-runs).
- Deleting a provider's last active credential under **Settings › AI providers** now lists the settings that still name the provider's models, which Tale no longer offers once the credential is gone: default models and model access, with how many rules or models; the vision, audio transcription and image generation models; the standard agent; and how many project agents. The delete still goes through and leaves those settings as they are, so choose other models for them afterwards. Under **Settings › Governance › Models**, **Default models** marks a rule whose provider or model is gone **(unavailable)** and says that such rules fall back to **Automatic** until you edit or remove them. **Model access** marks a model that no provider with an active credential offers any more, in the table and in the rule's model field. The field showed nothing for such a model before, so it could not be removed there; now it can ([#5340](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5340)). See [Rotate or retire credentials](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/admin/providers#rotate-or-retire-credentials) and [Models](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/admin/governance/content-models).
- A chat's title and a rewrite with **Improve with AI** in the Inbox now come only from a model that answers chat messages. Unless the person's own chat model can write them, Tale takes the first model by name that runs without thinking. An AI gateway lists its image models beside its chat models, so a gateway's image model, such as `gemini-3.1-flash-image`, could name a new chat. Tale now passes over such models there, as the chat's model picker already does. The hand check before v0.5.98's release found it.

## Upgrade notes

- This release adds no migration, to the application database or to the knowledge database, and the API contract stays at `3.52.0`.
- A task whose automatic starts a Claude Code 503 or 529 used up before the upgrade stays where it is, often **In progress** with no run. Start its agent again yourself: the hourly limit never refuses a person's own start.
- A gateway that answers Claude Code with 503 for a reason other than capacity now makes the task runs on that model wait too, for up to twelve hours, where they failed and were retried at once. When such runs read **Waiting for model capacity** for a long time, check the gateway.
- **Settings › Governance › Models** also marks **(unavailable)** what was left behind before the upgrade: a default-model rule whose provider has no active credential, and a model that no provider with an active credential offers any more. Such default-model rules already fell back to **Automatic**. Tale keeps all of them as saved until you edit or remove them.
- No configuration, limit, credential or sign-in setting needs to change beyond these: the other fixes take effect with the new images.
